To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the X-ray afterglow of gamma-ray bursts shows a wide variety of temporal and spectral behaviour, but that this diversity can be explained by a single underlying mechanism, the forward shock model, with energy injection continuing for days to weeks after the burst.
the X-ray light curves and spectra of GRB afterglows are consistent with a single model in which a relativistic jet interacts with the ambient medium and produces a forward shock.

(1) X-ray afterglows of GRBs show a variety of behaviours which can be described by a single underlying model; (2) the X-ray afterglow is consistent with forward shock synchrotron emission; (3) the afterglow emission requires energy injection to last for several days, which may indicate the presence of a central engine
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and interpretation of a large, uniform sample of X-ray data on GRBs.
the development of software tools to analyse Swift data, and the analysis of a complete, unbiased sample of GRB observations.
the analysis of the X-ray light curves of GRBs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a large sample of GRB light curves and spectra which are consistent with forward shock emission, but that we do not have a complete understanding of this process.
our data are inconsistent with the forward shock emission being the dominant component in the X-ray light curve of GRBs, but are consistent with the forward shock making only a small contribution.
we have not yet found the correct model for the prompt and X-ray afterglows of GRBs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the X-ray data are not inconsistent with the forward shock interpretation, but neither are they a strong confirmation.
the X-ray afterglow data of GRBs are consistent with the external shock model, but that the model requires significant revision to account for all the observations.
the XRT data are consistent with the forward shock emission model, but that the data do not strongly favour the model, and there are several difficulties to be overcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray light curves of GRBs can be understood in terms of a small set of parameters which are related in a simple way.
, despite the large sample size, the statistical uncertainties in the results of our study remain large.
the Swift-XRT data set represents a rich source of information about the nature of GRBs.
